subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Outdoor, Adventure, and Community Recreation Planning
title: Reteach and varied practice: risk assessment for an unfamiliar environment under transfer
focus: risk assessment for an unfamiliar environment
essentialQuestion: How do I plan an activity that is genuinely worth the effort of getting there?
privacySafeScenario: Produce a complete plan for one guardian-approved outdoor or community activity — risk assessment, logistics, contingency, and stewardship — and carry it out if approved, or complete the equivalent local or indoor version.
studentTask: Learner works risk assessment for an unfamiliar environment on a planned outing with a real contingency triggered, where the plan changes without the activity becoming unsafe at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of risk assessment for an unfamiliar environment degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds risk assessment for an unfamiliar environment on a planned outing with a real contingency triggered, where the plan changes without the activity becoming unsafe, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Scale, distance, terrain, and duration are learner-set. A full indoor or home-area equivalent is available for any learner for whom the outdoor activity is unsafe, inaccessible, or not approved.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of risk assessment for an unfamiliar environment yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Scale, distance, terrain, and duration are learner-set. A full indoor or home-area equivalent is available for any learner for whom the outdoor activity is unsafe, inaccessible, or not approved.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where risk assessment for an unfamiliar environment shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
